_comment_state: Set postgres (DSN) + redis (host:port) for multi-replica correctness: keys/spend in Postgres, rate limits + cache in Redis. Example: postgres://user@localhost:5432/llmux?sslmode=disable. For the sidecar the DSN is also read (later wins) from env LLMUX_POSTGRES, DATABASE_URL, then VULOS_DATABASE_URL (preferred shared Neon DSN). Embedders (core/gateway via config.FromJSON, and the C ABI) resolve differently: a value stated in the document wins over the environment, and the un-namespaced DATABASE_URL/VULOS_DATABASE_URL are not read at all, because in library mode those belong to the host application. When Postgres is used, tables live under postgres_schema (env LLMUX_POSTGRES_SCHEMA), default 'llmux', so llmux can share one database with other Vulos products.
_comment_cp: OPTIONAL Vulos control-plane integration. Leave cp_url empty for standalone (default: static keys, no cp). When set (or via env LLMUX_CP_URL / LLMUX_CP_SECRET) the gateway resolves identity, gates budget, and reports usage to cp via X-Relay-Auth. The core never imports the cp adapter; it is wired only by the binary.
_comment_cp_degraded: Degraded-mode posture when cp is unreachable AND no entitlement is cached (cold cache). DEFAULT bounds spend: requests are capped at cp_degraded_rpm per account per minute (0 = built-in conservative default of 20/min). Set cp_degraded_fail_open=true (or env LLMUX_CP_DEGRADED_FAIL_OPEN=1) to instead fail fully OPEN (unbounded) during a cp outage — only if you accept the spend risk.
_comment_byok: OPTIONAL per-account 'bring your own key'. When a 32-byte KEK is present (prefer env LLMUX_BYOK_KEK; raw 32 bytes, 64-char hex, or base64) accounts can register their OWN provider keys, encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM. A request for a provider the account has a BYOK key for is served with that key and is NOT metered or billed; everything else uses the central provider keys above and is metered. Manage keys via the master-key-gated PUT/DELETE/GET /admin/byok/{account}[/{provider}]. Leave kek empty to disable BYOK (every request uses central keys). See docs/LLM-ACCESS.md.
_comment_sovereignty: SOVEREIGNTY GATE: by default llmux only calls model backends that run on THIS box (loopback / unix-socket base URLs, e.g. Ollama or llama.cpp — classified 'local'). Any provider whose base_url is a remote endpoint ('egress') is DENIED at dispatch with a 403 sovereignty_error and never dialed — nothing leaves the box unless you say so. To permit a specific remote/brokered endpoint, set "allow_egress": true on that provider (explicit + logged/labeled). A local backend is also auto-detected from OLLAMA_HOST or LLMUX_LOCAL_BASE_URL as a passthrough provider named 'local', and becomes the catch-all route when no routes are configured. See core/sovereign.

providers.name: local
providers._comment: On-box sovereign default (Ollama/llama.cpp OpenAI-compatible server). Loopback => always allowed, no opt-in needed.

providers.name: openai
providers._comment: Remote => BLOCKED unless allow_egress is set.
